### Direction taken and why — PR #638 body

> ## Summary
>
> - Closes #637. The standing no-size-reduction rule was enforced by a text match: any string carrying vocabulary from a word list hit a HARD NO with no precondition to clear it. The rule is right; the TEST was wrong, in the same way #618's git guard was wrong — matching vocabulary instead of the operation.
> - New `.claude/hooks/lib/reduction-intent.ts` classifies what a string is DOING with its vocabulary, in four passes of decreasing structural certainty: (1) command syntax, parsed with the shared #629 tokenizer so a word is judged by POSITION rather than presence; (2) identifiers — snake_case, dotted, SQL grammar, JSON keys, file paths; (3) attributed speech — quotation spans carrying a speaker marker; (4) grammar — proposing (modal, imperative, interrogative offering a size) versus reporting (indicative about an existing subject, conventional-commit prefixes, bookkeeping cleanup).
> - **The teeth do not weaken.** Anything undecided after all four passes is a PROPOSAL and is refused. All 12 agent-voice proposals in the true-positive corpus are still refused, including the three 2026-07-30 originals, and the pre-existing gate regression suite stays at 31/31.
> - Two deliberate non-bypasses: quoted command arguments are NOT stripped, so prose smuggled into a commit message is still judged as prose; and an UNATTRIBUTED quotation is not exempt, so quote marks are not a one-character bypass.
> - Non-goals honored: the destructive-delete gate, fast-tools gate, and git guard (#618) are untouched, and no refusal message text or standing rule text changed.

>
> The check is two-sided on purpose. Passing every false positive is trivially achieved by deleting the wall; refusing every true positive is trivially achieved by refusing everything. Only the conjunction means anything, and a true-positive regression fails the whole run. True-positive refusals additionally assert the refusal did NOT come from an unrelated clause, so a block for the wrong reason cannot bank a false pass.
>
> Python package checks are not applicable: no file under `python/` is touched. Live smoke is not applicable: repo-local hooks are developer tooling and reach no server, database, or MCP surface.

> ## Critical Self-Review
>
> - Highest-risk behavior: a false PASS on a genuine agent-authored reduction proposal, which would let silent data loss through the one wall built to stop it. Mitigated by fail-closed defaulting on undecidable text and by 12 varied true-positive fixtures, but the classifier now reasons about grammar, and grammar has more surface than a word list.
> - Assumptions that could be wrong: that conventional-commit prefixes reliably mark a landed change rather than a proposal (an agent could write `chore(memory): cap the pack` and the prefix rule would classify it as reporting — the vocabulary still has to survive passes 1-3, but this is the thinnest of the four passes); that attribution markers are present whenever the operator is quoted; that proposing-beats-reporting on ties covers mixed sentences.
> - Missing/weak tests: no fixture exercises a proposal wearing a conventional-commit prefix, which is the specific bypass the previous bullet names. No fixture covers a non-English or heavily abbreviated proposal. The corpus is 28 hand-written cases, not a sample of real traffic.
> - Security/permission risk: none directly — no auth, namespace, or SQL path is touched. Indirect only, in that this file is a guard and a weakened guard is a risk to data integrity rather than to access control.
> - Migration/deploy risk: none. No schema, no migration, no service. Hooks are read from the working tree.
> - Downstream client/runtime risk: none. Per `docs/downstream-rollout.md` this is repo-local developer tooling with no MCP tool, schema, protocol, or client-facing surface; rtech-mcps, mcp2cli, and rtech-hermes are unaffected.
> - Rollback/cleanup concern: revert is a single commit and the previous behavior returns whole. The lane worktree and its detached clean-clone worktree are removed at teardown; scratch is archived, never deleted.
> - Fixes made before PR: two self-caught defects. (1) The driver first asserted only one refusal banner, and the RED run showed seven true positives "refused by the WRONG clause" when a sibling clause had refused them correctly — fixing that assertion instead of the sibling avoided a fix aimed at a layer that was never broken. (2) Adding path-stripping to the identifier pass regressed a defect-report fixture by deleting the subject noun its grammar needed; the grammar pass now reads the pre-stripped text, because stripping is for detection and classification must read the sentence as written.
> - Known residual risk: the conventional-commit-prefix rule is the widest single exemption added here and the likeliest future false pass. It is flagged rather than removed because refusing every commit message was one of the two taxes #637 was filed about; a narrower rule that also lets legitimate cleanup commits through is worth a follow-up.
